content.standfirst: The AI company says junior employees make up a smaller share of its technical teams than in early 2025, while meeting time has risen. Its internal report offers a snapshot of one AI-heavy workplace, not proof of how AI will change hiring across the economy.

sources.originalTitle: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings

segments.body: Anthropic’s report says the share of junior-level employees in technical departments fell from 21% to 14% since early 2025, and the share of junior technical hires dropped from 27% to 9%. The company links some change to coding tools that let non-technical staff build software, but also cites the normal expansion of other business functions.

segments.title: More output, more coordination
segments.body: Anthropic reports increases in code per person, sales per representative and contracts processed, but cautions that more code does not necessarily mean better code or business impact. Meeting time per employee rose 20% over the year. Some employees said AI shifted their work toward managing its output, which the company describes as creating a new demand on human attention and judgement.

content.headline: England's World Cup hopes suffer after 30-12 defeat by Tonga
content.shortHeadline: England lose 30-12 to Tonga in World Cup opener
content.standfirst: England must win their next two matches to keep a realistic chance of reaching the semi-finals after a costly, error-strewn opening defeat. Coach Brian McDermott says he can address the mistakes.

sources.originalTitle: McDermott seeks fix as England fight to save their World Cup

segments.body: England were beaten 30-12 by Tonga in their Rugby League World Cup opener in Perth. Handling errors, needless offloads and penalties repeatedly handed momentum to a Tonga side packed with Australian NRL players.

segments.title: A narrow path to the semi-finals
segments.body: Coach Brian McDermott said England were not outplayed tactically and that the errors could be fixed. They need to beat France next Saturday and Papua New Guinea on 30 October to have a realistic chance of progressing; results elsewhere could still decide their fate.

content.headline: Kartal reaches Wuhan final after two tie-break wins over Ostapenko
content.shortHeadline: Kartal beats Ostapenko to reach Wuhan final
content.standfirst: Sonay Kartal saved six set points and won two tie-breaks to reach the biggest final of her career, in only her third tournament since returning from a six-month injury absence.

image.caption: Sonay Kartal has reached the Wuhan Open final.

sources.originalTitle: Kartal reaches Wuhan final as dream week continues

segments.body: Kartal beat former French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) in the Wuhan semi-final. She recovered from trailing 4-1 in both sets and saved three set points in each, showing the composure she said made it one of the toughest matches of her career.

segments.title: A career milestone
segments.body: The world number 170 is the lowest-ranked player to reach a WTA 1,000 final since the format began in 1990. She will face Maja Chwalinska on Sunday; reaching the final also means Kartal is set to return to the world's top 50 and become Britain's number one when rankings are released on Monday.

content.headline: Manchester City beat Ipswich to go six points clear amid fan defiance
content.shortHeadline: City go six clear as fans boo Premier League anthem
content.standfirst: City made it seven league wins from seven under Enzo Maresca, with Erling Haaland scoring twice against Ipswich. Supporters also made their anger at the Premier League clear after the club's appeal over financial-rule findings.

image.caption: Erling Haaland celebrates after scoring twice against Ipswich.

sources.originalTitle: Boos and bananas on day of defiance at Man City

segments.body: Manchester City beat Ipswich to move six points clear at the top of the Premier League. Haaland scored twice, while Phil Foden also found the net on his return to the side; City have won all seven league matches under Enzo Maresca.

segments.title: A pointed show of support
segments.body: Before kick-off, City fans booed the Premier League anthem and waved inflatable bananas in the club's first home league game since a commission found it guilty of financial-rule breaches. City have appealed the findings, and Maresca said the club, players and supporters were united.

content.headline: Chelsea beat Everton as Martinez is taken to hospital for tests
content.shortHeadline: Chelsea win at Everton as Martinez goes to hospital
content.standfirst: Chelsea won 2-0 for their first league clean sheet in nine months, but goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez was taken to hospital after a collision. His condition and availability remain uncertain pending tests.

sources.originalTitle: Chelsea's Martinez taken to hospital for 'precautionary tests'

segments.body: Pedro Neto scored twice as Chelsea beat Everton 2-0, ending a run of 23 Premier League matches without a clean sheet. Everton managed just six shots, their fewest in a league game since last December.

segments.title: Martinez awaits test results
segments.body: Martinez collided with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite while trying to claim a cross and left the field after an eight-minute stoppage. Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said the goalkeeper had left the stadium conscious and was in hospital for precautionary tests; he said more was not yet known.

content.headline: Canada end England's 41-match unbeaten run with late try
content.shortHeadline: Canada end England's unbeaten run with late win
content.standfirst: Shoshanah Seumanutafa scored three minutes from time as Canada beat the world champions 24-21 in Toronto. England coach John Mitchell urged his side to respond after their first defeat since 2022.

image.caption: Canada's late fightback ended England's unbeaten run.

sources.originalTitle: England's 41-match unbeaten run ended by Canada

segments.body: England led 14-5 at half-time, but Canada fought back and Seumanutafa's late try completed a 24-21 win in front of a record 18,621 crowd for a standalone women's rugby match in North America. The result ended England's 41-match unbeaten run.

segments.title: England must respond
segments.body: Mitchell said there were good elements in England's performance but challenged the team to find more. Captain Meg Jones called for the squad to stick together. The teams meet again in Ottawa on 23 October before England face the USA in their final WXV Global Series match.

content.headline: Liverpool come from behind to beat nine-man Brentford as Wirtz shines
content.shortHeadline: Wirtz creates nine chances as Liverpool beat Brentford
content.standfirst: Liverpool recovered from their first league defeat of the season with a 2-1 win at Brentford, who finished with nine players. Florian Wirtz created chances in record-setting numbers, though questions remain about the team's balance.

image.caption: Liverpool came from behind to beat nine-man Brentford.

sources.originalTitle: Wirtz delivers but remains Liverpool's conundrum

segments.body: Liverpool scored twice in the second half to come from behind and beat Brentford 2-1 after the hosts had been reduced to nine men. Wirtz was central to the comeback, creating nine chances from open play—the most in a Premier League match in the past six seasons.

segments.title: Praise and a tactical question
segments.body: Wirtz has faced criticism after a difficult start to the league campaign, but he has now assisted in back-to-back games across all competitions. Former Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy praised the win while arguing that the midfield shape leaves too much space and could make the side vulnerable against stronger opposition.

content.headline: Manzambi's winner gives Aston Villa a 1-0 victory at Newcastle
content.shortHeadline: Manzambi scores winner as Villa beat Newcastle
content.standfirst: Johan Manzambi headed the only goal against the club he turned down to join Villa. The win extends Aston Villa's unbeaten run in all competitions to five matches after a difficult start to their league campaign.

image.caption: Johan Manzambi scored the winner for Aston Villa at Newcastle.

sources.originalTitle: Villa's Manzambi shows Newcastle what they missed out on

segments.body: Manzambi scored an unmarked header from Joao Gomes' cross to give Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Newcastle. The midfielder had turned down Newcastle before moving to Villa in a deal worth just over £50m, and has now scored three times for his new club.

segments.title: Villa building momentum
segments.body: The victory extended Villa's unbeaten run in all competitions to five matches and followed a 6-0 Champions League win over Fenerbahce. Manager Unai Emery said the team needed to rebuild confidence and consistency after taking one point from their first four league games.

content.headline: Connacht stun Saracens as Bath lose in Champions Cup openers
content.shortHeadline: Connacht stun Saracens as Bath and others fall
content.standfirst: Connacht scored seven tries to beat three-time champions Saracens, while Bath conceded 22 unanswered second-half points in defeat by Montpellier. Leinster and Munster opened their campaigns with wins.

image.caption: Lions players observe a minute's silence for Hyron Andrews.

sources.originalTitle: Seven-try Connacht beat Saracens in Champions Cup
Bath lose at home to Montpellier in Champions Cup
Seven-try Leinster too strong for Clermont

Tributes to Andrews before Champions Cup matches

segments.body: Connacht fought back from 12-0 down to beat Saracens in a seven-try contest, although the Irish side did not earn a bonus point. Bath led early in the second half against Montpellier but were outscored by 22 points without reply. Leinster also scored seven tries in a bonus-point win at Clermont, while Munster beat Racing 92 33-25.

segments.title: A match played in tribute
segments.body: The Lions played their Champions Cup match against La Rochelle in honour of team-mate Hyron Andrews, who died at the team's hotel on Friday aged 31. Tributes were paid before matches across the weekend; the Lions lost 31-14.
